open_points.subject: disclosure-class ordering
open_points.text: “the disclosure classes (A07 rule 1) and the effect classes (M10) are enumerations of `models`, each ordered by its declared order ... the members and the order have that one home” contradicts “`canonical_values` ... Owns ... The order of disclosure classes and the highest class of a set”
open_points.question: Does `models` own the disclosure-class order while `canonical_values` merely applies it, or does `canonical_values` own that order?
options: `models` owns the members and order; `canonical_values` owns only comparison and highest-class computation
open_points.default_guess: `models` owns the members and order; `canonical_values` reads that order to compute comparisons.

open_points.subject: port-value size validation
open_points.text: “any check that uses a ceiling ... belongs to the module whose rule it is” conflicts with “`canonical_values` ... Owns ... validation of a value against a port: presence, carriage, schema, size”
open_points.question: Which module owns selecting and enforcing the context-specific size ceiling when `fit_port_value` is used?
options: Each calling domain module owns its ceiling check; `canonical_values` checks only structural and schema fit
`canonical_values` owns size checks and callers supply the applicable ceiling
`canonical_values` chooses the applicable release ceiling itself
open_points.default_guess: Each calling domain module owns and performs its contextual ceiling check; `canonical_values` handles presence, carriage and schema fit.

open_points.subject: equal content submission behavior
open_points.text: “`canonical_values` ... Owns A01 rules 1 and 4” assigns it the rule that an existing identity returns the existing record unchanged, but `canonical_values` does not know `store` or the modules that issue those records
open_points.question: Which module owns enforcing A01 rule 4, including returning the existing record, preserving its first author and time, and not making an old version current again?
options: Each record-creating domain module owns the behavior, using an atomic store lookup/insert capability
`store` owns the behavior for every content-derived record
`canonical_values` gains access to persistence and owns the behavior
open_points.default_guess: Each record-creating domain module owns the behavioral consequences, while `store` provides atomic uniqueness by computed identity.

open_points.subject: pinned dependency and sandbox-runtime versions
open_points.text: “The pinned Python dependencies and sandbox runtime of A20 rule 3 are a release artifact built and checked outside the running kernel”
open_points.question: What named module or release component owns the exact dependency/runtime version list and verifies that the shipped release matches it?
options: A named release/build manifest and its verification step
open_points.default_guess: A checked-in release/build manifest with lock files owns the exact versions, and release verification checks the shipped artifacts against it.
